systemArchitectures.name: Commercial Continuous Focused-Microwave Atmospheric Cold Freeze-Drying & In-Line Lyophilization (FM-ACFD) Industrial Skid
systemArchitectures.classification: Continuous Aseptic Atmospheric Cryogenic Microwave Lyophilization Skid (FDA 21 CFR § 117 FSMA cGMP / 3-A Sanitary Standards 01-09 & 33-03 / EHEDG Type EL Class I CIP / FCC Title 47 Part 18 ISM Certified / ASME B31.3 Sanitary Piping)
systemArchitectures.technology: Continuous focused variable-frequency solid-state GaN microwave energy absorption (dual-band 2.45 GHz & 5.8 GHz, 150–600 W per cavity) coupled with atmospheric cold dry nitrogen fluidization (-20°C to -40°C, dew point < -60°C, atmospheric pressure 1.013 bar) for non-vacuum sublimation drying of heat-sensitive probiotic matrices, dairy enzymes, and infant formulas in under 45 minutes with >95% viable cell recovery.
systemArchitectures.microwaveFrequencyBands: Dual-Band Solid-State 2.45 GHz & 5.8 GHz GaN Power Amplifiers
systemArchitectures.fluidizingGasAtmosphere: 100% Ultra-High Purity Nitrogen (N2), Dew Point < -60°C, P = 1.013 bar (Non-Vacuum)
systemArchitectures.specificEnergyConsumptionSecKwhPerKg: 1.25 – 1.85 kWh/kg ice sublimated (vs 8.5–14.2 kWh/kg for vacuum lyophilization)
systemArchitectures.cipSanitizationRating: 100% Sanitary 316L Stainless Steel (Ra < 0.38 µm), EHEDG Type EL Class I CIP validated

formulations.name: Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG & Trehalose Cryo-Pellets
formulations.formulationDescription: Cryogenically frozen 2.5 mm spherical pellets of live probiotic Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG (10^10 CFU/g) stabilized with 10% D-trehalose and 2% skim milk solids.
formulations.degradingAlternative: Standard Vacuum Shelf Lyophilizer (48-hour batch cycle at 0.05 mbar with shelf radiant heating causing 38% loss in probiotic viability and high energy footprint)

formulations.name: Recombinant Thermolabile Fungal Lactase Matrix
formulations.formulationDescription: Ultra-pure fungal beta-galactosidase (lactase) frozen droplets in 8% maltodextrin cryo-protective carrier for lactose-free dairy formulations.
formulations.degradingAlternative: Convective Spray Drying (175°C inlet causing 74% irreversible thermal denaturation of enzyme active catalytic site)
formulations.regulatoryStandard: FDA GRAS Notice GRN 000572 & 3-A Sanitary Standard 33-03

formulations.name: Infant Formula HMO & Bifidobacterium infantis Complex
formulations.formulationDescription: 2'-fucosyllactose (2'-FL) HMO bioactive suspension formulated with live infant gut symbiont Bifidobacterium infantis EVC001.
formulations.degradingAlternative: Industrial Drum Drying (120°C heated rolls destroying 100% of live probiotic cells and caramelizing delicate HMO sugars)

formulations.name: Hyperimmune Bovine Colostrum Immunoglobulin G (IgG)
formulations.formulationDescription: First-milking bovine colostrum liquid concentrate rich in biologically active Immunoglobulin G (IgG > 50 g/L) and lactoferrin.
formulations.degradingAlternative: Conventional Thermal Evaporation & Spray Drying (leading to IgG quaternary unfolding, disulfide aggregation, and 62% loss in neutralizing efficacy)
formulations.regulatoryStandard: USDA APHIS 9 CFR & Pasteurized Milk Ordinance (PMO) Appendix N

formulations.name: Fresh Royal Jelly 10-HDA & Major Royal Jelly Protein (MRJP)
formulations.formulationDescription: Native fresh royal jelly emulsion preserving bioactive 10-hydroxy-2-decenoic acid (10-HDA) and apalbumin-1 glycoprotein.
formulations.degradingAlternative: Rotary Vacuum Evaporator (causes foaming collapse, phase separation, and 45% degradation of bioactive apalbumin glycoproteins)

formulations.name: Microwave Cavity Plasma Arcing & Ice Melt Collapse Hazard Mode
formulations.formulationDescription: Hazard baseline simulation: excessive electric field strength (|E| > 2.5 kV/cm), nitrogen dew point failure (T_dp > -20°C), runaway dielectric heating (ice melting into high-loss water), and localized plasma micro-discharges.
formulations.degradingAlternative: Catastrophic dielectric breakdown, localized nitrogen plasma arcing scorch, runaway ice melting into boiling liquid, and collapse of porosity
formulations.regulatoryStandard: NON-COMPLIANT: FCC Title 47 Part 18 RF Hazard & Severe Biological Denaturation
